Alex.regret: In round 1 I piled onto Blair with my Wild after calling them out, and Blair was Farm, which handed Meowfia the round. I would have held off the accusation until more evidence came in.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's report: I misread it as showing visitors to me, when it showed visitors to my target, and I misstated it on day one. The confused dawn report in round 3 also left me unsure of my own losses.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Finley's Hawk egg and Alex's Owl report both pointed at Drew, and the table converged on a Mouser in one day.
Blair.change: I would make the confused-report rule clearer, so players know exactly what a confused dawn report looks like and can flag it cleanly.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey on a suspicion built on a Kookaburra read I already knew was unreliable. I would hold low cards and stay out of that vote instead.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit reporting was hard to track, and I misread my own Eagle mechanic at first, which caused a needless dispute with Blair. Blair's -2 in round 3 never got explained, so the egg-loss sources were unclear.
Casey.fun: Drew's Mouser visit to Ellis was exposed by Alex's Owl report, and Finley's Hawk egg confirmed it, so the round 2 vote felt like a solid deduction.
Casey.change: Dawn reports could name each visitor's animal when an egg is gained or lost, so players could check claims without guessing.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Blair, a Farm Kookaburra, on the strength of an unexplained egg loss, and my cards were discarded. I'd keep my cards and wait for a clearer read on who was actually hitting Blair.

Drew.confusing: The dawn reports didn't say who visited whom, so egg-count claims like Casey's Eagle +2 were hard to verify. Confused players also got wrong information with no clear way to tell.
Drew.fun: Watching the table pile onto Blair's Owl story, then seeing Casey's and Ellis's claims line up, made the day feel like a real puzzle.
Drew.change: Include each visitor's identity in the dawn report so egg-count claims can be checked directly.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair, a Farm player, and that helped Meowfia win. I should have held my cards or thrown at the player whose claim didn't add up, instead of joining the early pile-on.

Ellis.confusing: Dawn confusion was hard to read: my Kookaburra report on Drew said House Cat while I was confused, and I could not tell which dawn reports were reliable. Blair's -2 also looked like a contradiction I could not trace.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Meowfia Floofer, I hugged Blair and blended in with a Tit claim while the table argued over Casey's Eagle count.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited you, so confusion does not hide the truth from honest Farm players.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw my Wild at Blair, a Farm player, based on the table's story; I should have waited for more evidence, since the real Meowfia were Alex and Drew.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track: Blair's dawn report was wrong, but I couldn't tell which of their claims to trust, and their story kept shifting.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk egg from visiting Drew exposed them as Meowfia and the table voted them out, which Farm won with my three-card throw.
Finley.change: I'd make it clearer when a dawn report is confused, so players know whether a claim is unreliable.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I threw my Wild at Blair on a wording argument, and Blair was Farm, so my vote helped Ellis's Floofer side win. I should have pressed Ellis's Tit claim and Alex's Hawk claim harder before voting.</regret>

review.title: The Wasted Wink
review.headline: Finley banked a 19-point round, then the table voted out the wrong Farmer.
review.summary: Round 1 was a fog of Farm claims. The table piled onto Blair over a misread Owl rule, and the lone Meowfia, Ellis, won without lifting a finger. Round 2 was clean. Alex's Owl and Finley's Hawk both pointed at the Mouser, Drew, and Farm won. Finley banked a huge pile. In round 3 a confused Kookaburra report made Blair look like a liar. The Meowfia winked the leader and let Farm eggsecute Blair. Finley still won by 12 points.

rounds.recap: Ellis was the only Meowfia, a Floofer who hugged Blair. Blair's Owl wording shifted because she misread her own rule. Everyone but Casey piled onto her with cheap throws, and Farm lost. Ellis gained 3 points for doing nothing.

Drew, a Mouser, winked Ellis in the day, which exposed that a Mouser exists. Alex's Owl saw only a Mouser visit Ellis, and Drew admitted visiting Ellis. Finley's Hawk egg also pointed at Drew. Three CAWs came fast and Drew was eggsecuted. Finley threw three mid cards and banked 19.

Alex (Mouser) and Drew (Floofer) were the Meowfia. Alex winked Finley, the runaway leader, early. Blair's confused Kookaburra report named Finley as House Cat, and her -2 eggs had no source. Casey's Owl and Ellis's Falcon backed Finley's Eagle, so Farm voted Blair. Blair was Farm, and the Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Alex's Owl report of only a Mouser visiting Ellis, plus Drew's own admitted visit, let Farm solve the round in one beat.
Finley's Hawk egg from visiting Drew was near-proof. Finley called it out and threw three cards at Drew, banking 19 points.
Alex used the Wink on Finley, the 23-point leader, before the first vote. It was a smart play on the standings and not on the round.
Blair misread the Owl and then the Eagle. The table spent a whole day punishing a rules mistake instead of a lie.

confusions.what: Thought the Owl learns visitors to herself, then to her target. She changed her story and looked guilty.
Said Casey's +2 needed two visitors to Casey. She misread how the Eagle gains eggs.
Her day statement was muddled. Casey had to correct that Casey visited Blair, not Alex.
Said Blair's Owl should have shown visitors to Blair. The Owl reports visitors to her target.
Treated Blair's -2 as proof she was lying. Casey ignored that the Kookaburra's confusion can change an egg count. Casey's own Owl saw only the Eagle visit Blair.
Called Alex's Owl claim 'new' as if roles should persist between rounds.
Said 'only a cat can be a Mouser' as if the Owl names players. It names animals, and her logic only worked because Drew volunteered the visit.
As Kookaburra she lost 2 eggs and was told Drew is the House Cat. She was confused, but Drew was a Mouser.

worked: Owl and Hawk cross-checks in round 2 gave clean, checkable evidence. The Mouser/Owl report matched the admitted visit and the Hawk egg.
Throw counts as public signals mattered. Finley's three-card throw and the cheap Wild throws all read as confidence or caution.
The Wink on the leader gave the Meowfia a real strategic decision. It tied the standings into the round.
The consolation rule gave Drew a reason to throw at Finley in round 2 and Casey in round 3, which is a sensible hedge.
problems: Confused reports make Farm look like liars with no way to check. In round 3 the Kookaburra's confused report cost Farm the round. Consider letting a confused player see that they were confused, and let the Storyteller say which stat is wrong.
The runaway lead is decisive. Finley's 19-point round made rounds 3 irrelevant for first place. Cap the banked value per round, or reduce the cards a player can bank.

Day talk is mostly cheap Farm claims with little bluffing. In round 1 the lone Meowfia just copied a safe claim and won. A single Meowfia is almost uncatchable when the Floofer hugs a role that nobody can verify.
Rules misreads on the Owl and Eagle drove the round 1 vote. The card text could say 'visitors to the player you visited' more plainly.
Throws are mostly Wilds and low cards, so the vote is rarely costly. Round 1 and 3 throws had no real stakes. Raise the minimum throw or the value of the cards returned to the nest.
